disposition: NOT LANDED, and for the FIRST TIME IN FOUR ROUNDS the failure is not purely prose: one of the two blockers is a code defect this round introduced. The reviewer says plainly what is now proven, because seven rounds of failure have made that hard to see: the approach is confirmed for a fifth time, the KIND test remains a complete partition, all four round-7 blockers are genuinely closed and each was reproduced here on the shipped code, the 105-shape differential reproduces ROW FOR ROW with zero mismatches, the locale fix reproduces to the digit, the read_text sweep is the whole class rather than a sample, the teeth grew from 42 to 43 correctly with the new guard verified load-bearing by hand, and the recursion fails CLOSED on every unreadable, permission-denied, non-regular and record-bearing shape this reviewer could construct. What it does not survive is DEPTH: RecursionError is not an OSError, so the one error the new code path can raise is the one error it does not fail closed on, and it takes all four surfaces down exactly as the byte R6-B1 blocked on did - under a spec clause that says the proof holds AT ANY DEPTH and a gate label that repeats it over a fixture two levels deep. THE METHOD LESSON THIS ROUND ADDS, because 'enumerate the domain of the universal' was necessary and not sufficient: WHEN A UNIVERSAL QUANTIFIES OVER AN UNBOUNDED DOMAIN, ENUMERATION IS IMPOSSIBLE AND THE SENTENCE NEEDS A BOUND IN THE CODE, NOT A LARGER SAMPLE. 'At any depth', 'any size', 'any number of entries' and 'any length' are not claims a fixture can back at all; each one is a resource limit waiting to be found, and the fail-closed default only holds for the exceptions the code names. The second lesson is smaller and sharper: an accounting that says NO ASSERTION WAS DELETED is itself a universal, and this round's was checked against 8 of its 12 members - so the document proving the rule was followed is the one place the rule was not. The remaining work is ONE code change (a declared depth bound returning False, or RecursionError caught at .warp/metrics_read_accounting.py:209) and five sentences, and it is under an hour.
